title: Prefill latency prober and kernel-aware stage watermarking
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight prefill latency prober that adapts stage watermarks and selects kernel variants at runtime to reduce tail latency and improve KV cache hotness. Backpressure signaling between stages prevents prefill bursts from overwhelming decode. No API changes.
description:
Summary: Introduces a runtime component (prefill-latency-prober) that samples per-stage service time distributions and uses those signals to dynamically adjust the prefill/decode watermark boundary and pick kernel variants optimized for the current workload (e.g., quantified kernels for throughput vs fp16 for latency-sensitive slices). Motivation: We observed intermittent tail spikes when prefill burstiness interacted poorly with decode-stage kernel selection and KV cache priming, particularly across mixed-length workloads. Static stage boundaries and one-size-fits-all kernel choices were causing decode-stage stalls or unnecessary kernel overhead. This change reduces 95th/99th p95/p99 for mixed workloads in our internal canary by up to 18% and lowers end-to-end token cost in throughput runs by ~4%.

Details:
- New component: runtime/prefill_prober
  - Periodically samples request latency at prefill and decode boundaries using lightweight probes injected into ongoing batches; maintains sliding histograms (configurable window) of observed service times.
  - Computes a moving watermark that defines how far prefill can progress ahead of decode without increasing tail risk; watermark aims to keep decode KV cache warm while avoiding large decode backlogs.
  - Emits metrics (probe.latency.percentiles, probe.watermark, probe.kernel_hint) for Console and SLO monitoring.
- Kernel selection adapter
  - runtime/kernel_adapter reads kernel_hint from the prober and switches kernel families for decode micro-slices when safe (non-blocking switch on kernel warmup). Supports quantized and fp16 variants; plumbs minimal compatibility metadata to ensure KV cache layout compatibility.
- Backpressure wire between prefill and decode
  - Adds a bounded credit channel and explicit backpressure messages so prefill can gracefully stall when decode cannot keep up; implements priority fast-path for interactive slices (low-entropy prompts) to bypass credit delays when SLO demands.
- Micro-slicing refinement
  - When watermark indicates increased risk of tail spikes, prefill will opportunistically emit smaller micro-slices to improve scheduling granularity and reduce per-slice variance seen by decode.
- Safety and opt-out
  - Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_prefill_prober`. Default off in private deployments; on in hosted canaries. Telemetry sanitized, and kernel switches require model compatibility matrix entry.

Checklist:
- [x] Prober implementation + unit tests for histogram/windowing
- [x] Kernel adapter and compatibility checks
- [x] Backpressure integration with existing prefill scheduler
- [x] Benchmarks: microbench harness and canary results attached
- [x] Docs update in runtime/README describing new flags and metrics

Benchmarks & results: See attached pipeline-run summaries in commits. Canary on 64-gpu cluster with mixed short/long prompts: p95 latency reduced ~12-18% across models tested; throughput runs (sustained) saw token-cost drop ~3-5% when kernel_adapter chose quantized paths for heavy throughput slices.

Commit summary: short, focused commits described below.

Related: ENG-3121 (prefill tail incidents), ENG-3402 (kernel warmup roadmap).

review_comments: Ethan Liu (2026-02-13): Can we avoid switching kernel families mid-request? Author: the kernel_adapter performs non-blocking warmup and only switches at micro-slice boundaries; added compatibility checks to ensure KV layout remains stable.

Marina Gomez (2026-02-14): The histogram window may hide transient spikes. Author: window size is configurable and defaulted conservatively; added a short-term outlier detector to react faster to sudden regressions.

Ravi Krishnan (2026-02-15): Watch memory pressure from smaller micro-slices. Author: micro-slice creation uses object pooling and we added a stress test that simulates fragmentation; numbers look acceptable under our canary workloads.
Ethan Liu (2026-02-16): CI flaked on integration test; reran and all green now.
notes_for_ops: Toggle 'enable_prefill_prober' feature flag to controlled canaries first. Monitor probe.latency.percentiles and probe.watermark dashboards; if p99 regresses, rollback flag. Kernel switching relies on entries in models/compat/kernel_compat_matrix.yaml - ensure model onboarding includes compatibility metadata.
